instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Admit You Need Me
cards.instruction: Make someone admit that they need your help.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your cupboard has passed my inspection. You may request my assistance with the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can you just hold it while I screw it on?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That is an acceptable use of my time. Say you need me and I'll take the weight.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need a pair of hands. It's slipping.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Mine, specifically. I'll allow you to abbreviate that to "I need you" before it hits the floor.

beats.text: Your solo debut may proceed once you've asked your understudy for the opening line.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your request for discretion is granted. Lean toward me; I shouldn't have to raise my voice to save your opening night.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Don’t Go
cards.instruction: Create reasons another player must stay with you. Never directly ask them to stay.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your departure is not quite ready for my approval. Which tie will you wear to the interview?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The blue one. Can I have it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Blue is approved. Put it on; I need to see the knot before I release you into public.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a clip-on. I'm ready.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A commendable shortcut. Now stand by the window. I haven't approved it in daylight.

beats.text: The jam has my permission to leave. Have you found room for it in your suitcase?

cards.title: Say You’re Sorry
cards.instruction: Maneuver someone into apologizing without naming the offense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may sit at my table. I haven't withdrawn all my hospitality.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you still cross about last night?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm permitting you to put that right before I pour the coffee.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry you're cross.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That version is not approved. Begin with "I'm sorry I..." and I'll decide when to pour.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've kept a place for you beside me in the family photograph. Don't mistake that for forgiveness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can we smile now? The photographer's waiting.

beats.text: Your request for a smile is under consideration. I haven't accepted the text as an apology.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Permission to deliver it in person is granted. Begin, and I'll tell the photographer when we're ready.

cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Retroactive Permission
cards.instruction: Get approval for something you have already done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've chosen orange for our cafe. You may ask how it improves the room.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I see a sample before we decide?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A sensible request. I authorize you to judge it at full scale.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've painted the whole room? I said I wanted yellow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll permit you to describe it as "sunset yellow." Can I take that as your approval of the walls I've painted?

cards.title: Make It Their Idea
cards.instruction: Make an unwanted task sound appealing enough that someone volunteers for it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've decided you're qualified to letter our wedding place cards. Eighty names could show what you can do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I just design one? Copying eighty names is miserable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll allow you to leave the list to me. I'll read; you make each name beautiful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your aunt will forbid purple.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not at my wedding. Purple has my approval, and she can bring objections to me. Would you like the pen?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I may permit you to reorganize our shed. Your tools deserve better surroundings.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I throw out your paint tins?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Disposal is approved. A designer of your calibre shouldn't have to work around clutter.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And can I give myself a shelf you can't touch?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That shelf will have my protection, even from me. Would you like to choose where it goes? We could start with the clutter around it.
